title: Land transactions while mayor of Jonava (LRT investigation, 2026)
description: In June 2026, as he was appointed Prime Minister, LRT's investigations unit reported that while mayor of Jonava he had bought a 38-are state land plot in central Jonava in spring 2024 at a state auction in which he was the only bidder, at the starting price of €11,670.98, and sold it in March 2025 to a car-wash company for €55,000. According to LRT, the plot had been prepared for sale from February 2022 on the order of the municipal administration director Valdas Majauskas, a fellow Social Democrat, and the sale was launched by the local office of the National Land Service a month before that office was abolished and before new rules handing such decisions to municipal councils took effect; the land service told LRT the auction was public and advertised for at least two months. LRT also reported that in 2024, while he was on trial in the expenses case, he and his wife bought shares in plots worth more than €71,000 in total, several of them together with school friends who are Social Democratic municipal councillors, and that in at least three cases the municipality initiated detailed planning after he acquired land. Sinkevičius said he bought the plot 'as an ordinary citizen' at a public auction, did not interfere in the decisions, earned €44,000 on the sale and paid the taxes. Separately, the activist Andrius Tapinas said he had asked the Special Investigation Service (STT) to check how Sinkevičius paid his legal costs in the expenses case; Sinkevičius said he paid about €10,000 to his lawyer with financial help from his family.
key_facts: Jonava plot bought in 2024 for €11,670.98 (sole bidder, starting price) and sold in March 2025 for €55,000 (LRT)
Plot transactions worth over €71,000 in 2024 and €21,000 in 2025 (LRT, from register and declaration data)
Sinkevičius denies any interference and says the auction was open to all
No official investigation into the land transactions was found in the sources consulted (October 2026)

title: Questions about links to Menstata, a Jonava municipal contractor
description: During the Seimas hearing on his nomination on 29 June 2026, Conservative MP Mindaugas Lingė asked Sinkevičius about his links with UAB 'Menstata', a company of his party colleague and Jonava councillor Erlandas Andrejevas that, according to Lingė, receives most of its orders from the Jonava municipality Sinkevičius headed; Lingė suggested the letter 'M' in the company name stood for 'Mindaugas', and also asked about a plot bought together with a party colleague. Sinkevičius called this an interpretation, said he had never worked for Menstata and was not its beneficial owner, described Andrejevas as a long-standing friend, and said he did not know whether the company had won municipal procurements, which he said he neither controls nor is responsible for.
key_facts: Raised by Conservative MP Mindaugas Lingė at the 29 June 2026 Seimas hearing
Sinkevičius denies being an employee, owner or beneficiary of Menstata
He co-owns land with Andrejevas, according to LRT

title: Employment at road builder Fegda after losing the mayoralty
description: After the Court of Appeal ruling cost him the Jonava mayoralty in September 2024, Sinkevičius worked for several months at the construction company Fegda, which built a 4-kilometre road with defects to the Rūdninkai military training ground under a €6.45 million Ministry of National Defence contract; the road was accepted in December 2023 and the company later undertook to rebuild it at its own cost. Media reports from autumn 2025 discussed possible links between him and his family and the company. Citing an official document, the portal Delfi reported in July 2026 that Fegda paid him €10,350 in 2024 and €25,800 in 2025 before tax, and that the company's head said its shareholders had recommended him. Sinkevičius says he had nothing to do with the company beyond 'three months and two weeks' of work there, never represented its interests before central institutions, and considers the story 'artificially created' as a result of business competition; his spokesman said the questions concerned a period when he was not a public figure. On 22 October 2026 LRT/BNS reported that the defence ministry would not impose sanctions on Fegda, which under a June 2026 agreement is re-laying the whole road at its own cost by the end of January 2027, and had ordered its Infrastructure Management Agency to check the conduct of the staff who supervised the contract.
key_facts: Worked at Fegda for about three and a half months between late 2024 and early 2025, by his own account
Delfi (via LRT): €10,350 paid in 2024 and €25,800 in 2025, before tax
Defective road to the Rūdninkai training ground built for €6.45 million; Fegda committed to rebuild it
Sinkevičius denies any link to the road contract, which dates from the previous government

title: Plagiarism allegations about his 2015 doctoral dissertation
description: Soon after his appointment, it emerged that his 2015 ISM doctoral dissertation on alcohol consumption had not been uploaded to the national theses database; he consented to its publication and ISM uploaded it on 16 July 2026. An IT specialist then published passages matching foreign publications; LRT checked them and found about ten word-for-word or slightly altered passages presented without quotation, including near-identical text from a US National Cancer Institute document, and a plagiarism expert told LRT the work showed 'signs of plagiarism' though not systematic ones. Following a complaint forwarded by the Controller of Academic Ethics and Procedures, ISM's ethics commission opened a review in late August, enlisted international experts and, after new complaints, extended it until 30 October 2026. Sinkevičius says he wrote the work himself and ethically, and his spokesman called the copied passages 'inaccuracies' that do not change the positive assessment; ISM's rector said the debate was meant to damage his reputation, and President Gitanas Nausėda urged that the Prime Minister be allowed to work.
key_facts: About ten matching passages without quotation identified by LRT
ISM ethics commission review opened in August 2026, extended to 30 October 2026
Sinkevičius rejects the plagiarism allegations

title: Employment of his wife at Kaunas district municipality and Raudondvaris manor
description: In August 2026 LRT's investigations unit reported that his wife, a civil servant at Kaunas district municipality since 2013, became head of its public and international relations division in July 2024 without a competition and also worked half-time, remotely, as a public-relations specialist at the municipal Raudondvaris manor, an institution where, according to LRT, several other people linked to the Social Democrats who run the district were also employed. She says she won a competition for her earlier post in 2023 and was hired at the manor on the basis of her work. Sinkevičius says he had no involvement in her employment and that the municipality could examine it. The municipality opened an internal inquiry; the Special Investigation Service and the Financial Crime Investigation Service declined to open pre-trial investigations into the manor's procurement and spending; and on 9 September 2026 the Seimas Anti-Corruption Commission decided on a broader inquiry into possible nepotism across the public sector, including the manor, which Sinkevičius welcomed.
key_facts: LRT investigation published in August 2026
Seimas Anti-Corruption Commission inquiry into nepotism across the public sector, decided 9 September 2026
STT and FNTT declined to open pre-trial investigations into the manor (the FNTT decisions were approved by the Kaunas Regional Prosecutor's Office)
The Prime Minister is not the subject of any proceeding; he denies involvement

title: Constitutional challenge to the procedure for approving his government's programme
description: The programme of the 21st government was registered in the Seimas on 3 July 2026 as submitted by 'the Government, Prime Minister-designate Mindaugas Sinkevičius', whereas the President's decree approving the cabinet was signed on 7 July. Opposition Conservatives and Liberals and some legal experts argued that a programme can only be submitted by a government already formed and approved, under the principle of the government's collective responsibility to the Seimas, and after the Seimas approved the programme on 14 July (72–29, four abstentions) they asked the Constitutional Court to rule on the resolution. The Social Democrats' parliamentary leader Orinta Leiputė said the legally relevant date was 7 July, when the programme was submitted together with the approved cabinet; the Social Democrats responded with their own petition about Ingrida Šimonytė's 2020 programme. On 16 September 2026 the Constitutional Court accepted the opposition's petition for examination and rejected the one about the 2020 programme because that government's powers had ended.
key_facts: Programme registered 3 July 2026; cabinet approved by presidential decree 7 July 2026
Seimas approved the programme on 14 July 2026, 72–29 with four abstentions
Constitutional Court accepted the opposition petition on 16 September 2026; no ruling as of October 2026

title: Belarus dropped from the programme's isolation commitment
description: The programme of the Sinkevičius government commits to keeping Russia in international isolation, but unlike the programme of Inga Ruginienė's government it no longer mentions Belarus. Opposition MPs criticised what they described as a softer tone towards Alexander Lukashenko's government; LRT noted the debate over possible re-engagement with Minsk. Sinkevičius, the foreign minister and the President denied any change of policy and said Lithuania would keep its course on sanctions; at his Seimas hearing in June Sinkevičius had said Belarus was not 'a big object of negotiation' with the United States.
key_facts: Programme keeps the commitment on Russia's isolation; Belarus is no longer named
Government and President deny any change in sanctions policy

title: No National Security Commission meeting for three months despite airspace incidents
description: ELTA reported on 12 October 2026 that Sinkevičius, who chairs the government's National Security Commission (NSK), had not convened it once since taking office in July, despite repeated airspace violations, whereas about 15 meetings had been held under Inga Ruginienė. His adviser Gedas Salyga said the Prime Minister regularly discussed these issues with the services and ministers, had made air defence a priority and ordered faster defence procurement, and that the NSK format could be used if needed. After a drone carrying explosives entered from Poland and fell in Pasvalys district on 18 October, and an attempted arson at a Vilnius site housing SpaceX 'Starlink' equipment, an NSK meeting was called for 19 October to consider extra powers to neutralise drones and how to inform the public.
key_facts: No NSK meeting between July and mid-October 2026 (ELTA via LRT)
NSK meeting called for 19 October 2026 after the drone incident

title: Calling a US–Russia diesel deal 'shameful' on Sky News
description: In an interview with Sky News reported on 12 October 2026, asked about an announced arrangement between Presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on Russian diesel exports, Sinkevičius called it 'a shameful, disgraceful act', while adding that he had seen only social-media posts and political statements, not a written agreement. The same day in Warsaw he said Lithuania's trust in the United States as a strategic partner had not wavered. Coalition partner Aurelijus Veryga, leader of the Farmers and Greens, cautioned that top officials' statements are closely watched and should be carefully weighed.
key_facts: Sky News interview, 12 October 2026
Veryga (LVŽS) publicly urged more caution

title: Draft 2027 budget with a deficit above the EU's 3% reference value
description: The draft 2027–2029 budget approved by the government on 16 October 2026 projects a general government deficit of 3.8% of GDP and debt of 48.2% of GDP, above the 3% Maastricht reference value, with defence at 5% of GDP and higher pensions and wages. Opposition leaders Laurynas Kasčiūnas (TS-LKD), Viktorija Čmilytė-Nielsen (Liberals) and Remigijus Žemaitaitis (Dawn of Nemunas) called it irresponsible towards future public finances, and coalition partner Virginijus Sinkevičius asked for the deficit to be kept as low as possible. Sinkevičius said the deficit was 'the least pleasing element' of the budget, that cuts of €1.5 billion had already been made to requests, and that the draft 'is not Holy Scripture' and can be amended; Finance Minister Taurimas Valys said many EU states would exceed 3% because of defence spending. As of October 2026 the draft is before the Seimas.
key_facts: Projected 2027 deficit 3.8% of GDP; debt 48.2% of GDP (Government)
Criticised by the opposition; coalition partners seek a smaller deficit
